about: the Guiwei lychee cut across (objects/lychee/lychee.py --section), its cut face to the camera, under objects/lychee/recipes/rig_section.json, framed to the arc of the original's shot 4

camera.why: our choice: a 65 mm macro (as shot 19) looking 8 degrees down at the cut face; placed and focused so the pericarp's upper edge is the arc of the original's shot 4. f/256 renders a focus stack's depth (see focus_stack)

focus_stack.why: at 2.55x, f/8 holds 0.26 mm in focus and the rim is 1-2 mm deep, the face 2.4 mm in front of the arc: a macro photographer stacks slices at f/8. Stand-in: the render's lens is nearly a pinhole (f/256, all in focus) and the camera chain diffracts as one slice, at f/8 (1 + m) (objects/lychee/run.py writes optics.json)

render_why: 256 bounces: light crosses the aril (about 16 mm, mu_s about 1.7 /mm) by tens of scatterings, the pericarp's layers by more

develop.why: neutral curve; +0.5 EV: the exposure is set on the 99.9th percentile, which the juice's glints own

white_balance.why: our choice: balanced for 5000 K under the rig's 4000 K lamps, so the shot is warm (5500 made the rim orange)

mix_why: S4, toward the look target's numbers (bg 28,0,1; rim 192,69,66; flesh 211,181,149): rims carry the tubercles, the side pair the flesh and its glints, the top light the domes' upper flanks (higher, it turns the rim coral), the ground nearly off; a first guess, set after the render with the sheet
